unit_label: Temps (tense: passé composé vs imparfait, etc.)

blocks.note: Classify clean present-tense examples as current, timeless, habitual, future, or historical; exclude the open-ended synthetic film-outline task.

Choose present or imperfect for an ongoing interval introduced by depuis, and a completed past form when the event itself is over; exclude the one answer with competing interpretations and use the printed key because reconstructed solutions retain source blanks.

Use future, future perfect, conditional, or an appropriate past tense in time clauses according to the clause's actual temporal relation; exclude the three judgment-dependent translations and use the printed key because reconstructed solutions retain source blanks.

Distinguish ordinary earlier-past relations from immediate succession in literary and spoken registers, including the rare past-anterior and double-compound forms; use the printed key because reconstructed solutions retain source blanks.

First decide whether si means whether or introduces a condition, then apply reported-speech tense sequence or the no-future/no-conditional rule for hypothetical si clauses; exclude the one judgment-dependent item and use the printed key because reconstructed solutions retain source blanks.
